title: Design System: Cascade Web Design Truck-Door Livery

display.purpose: Business name (h1) and painted numerals (plate stats, star rating, step discs). Identity moments only.

headline.purpose: Section headings (h2), always led by the gold ▸ tick.

body.purpose: Running copy; weight climbs 500→700 for emphasis without changing face.

label.purpose: Short all-caps taglines and badges: since-chip, hero call lead-in, arc-lettered tagline, h1 subline.

shadows.name: signpainter-drop-shade
shadows.purpose: Default text-shadow for every display-face word; hard-edged and stacked, never blurred.

shadows.name: rivet-bolt-head
shadows.purpose: Small literal shadow under every rivet dot.

shadows.name: call-button-lift
shadows.purpose: Glossy raised-enamel edge on the call button only.

shadows.name: panel-settle
shadows.purpose: Applied only after a .reveal panel finishes animating in; the sole ambient container shadow.

shadows.name: tape-drop
shadows.purpose: Pre-purchase spec-preview ribbon shadow; untokenized, outside the enamel palette (see narrative notes).

motion.name: reveal-stagger-step
motion.purpose: Cascades elements that enter the viewport together; elements crossing alone settle immediately.

motion.name: glint-sweep
motion.purpose: One-shot specular highlight sweeping the hero call panel on load.

motion.name: shade-scroll-deepen
motion.value: rAF-throttled scroll listener, 0→2.5px added to h1 text-shadow offset as min(scrollY/600,1)*2.5
motion.purpose: Lettering shade deepens subtly with scroll, as if the door tilts away from the light.

components.name: Primary Button (Call)
components.description: The tel: call action. Appears in the sticky callbar, the hero doorframe, and the page finale.
components.html: (503) 246-5381
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:.55rem; background:linear-gradient(180deg,#f9601f 0%, var(--call,#ff5c1c) 45%, var(--call-deep,#c93f0d) 100%); color:#2e0e02; text-decoration:none; font-family:var(--body,'Barlow Semi Condensed',sans-serif); font-weight:700; font-size:1.05rem; letter-spacing:.03em; padding:.55rem 1.05rem; border-radius:6px; box-shadow:0 3px 9px rgba(0,0,0,.45), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.35); } .ds-btn-primary__icon { flex:none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter:brightness(1.06); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform:translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline:3px solid var(--gold,#c9a24b); outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Chip Badge
components.description: The "since/licensed" credential badge beneath the arc tagline. Rivet dots flank each side.
components.html: LICENSED ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR · SINCE 1977
components.css: .ds-chip { position:relative; display:inline-block; padding:.5rem 2.3rem; color:var(--gold,#c9a24b); font-family:var(--body,'Barlow Semi Condensed',sans-serif); font-weight:600; font-size:1.05rem; letter-spacing:.18em; border:1.5px solid var(--gold-dim,#8a7440); border-radius:8px; background:linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(27,50,82,.65), rgba(13,26,44,.65)); } .ds-chip__rivet { position:absolute; width:7px; height:7px; top:50%; margin-top:-3.5px; border-radius:50%; background:radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, #e8d9ae, var(--gold-dim,#8a7440) 70%, #5c4d27); box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.5); } .ds-chip__rivet--l { left:9px; } .ds-chip__rivet--r { right:9px; }

components.name: Trust Plate
components.description: One of three riveted stat cards under the hero (rating, founding year, permit count).
components.html:

components.css: .ds-plate { position:relative; background:radial-gradient(120% 90% at 30% 0%, var(--enamel-lit,#1b3252) 0%, var(--enamel,#14263e) 55%, var(--enamel-deep,#0d1a2c) 100%); border:1.5px solid var(--gold-dim,#8a7440); border-radius:10px; padding:1.05rem 1.1rem .95rem; text-align:center; } .ds-plate__big { font-family:var(--display,'Alfa Slab One',serif); font-size:1.55rem; color:var(--cream,#f3e9d5); text-shadow:1.5px 1.5px 0 var(--shade,#060d16); } .ds-plate__star { color:var(--gold,#c9a24b); } .ds-plate__small { color:var(--cream-dim,#cdbfa3); font-size:.98rem; font-weight:600; letter-spacing:.04em; margin-top:.15rem; } .ds-plate__rivet { position:absolute; width:8px; height:8px; border-radius:50%; background:radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, #e8d9ae, var(--gold-dim,#8a7440) 70%, #5c4d27); box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.5); } .ds-plate__rivet--tl { top:7px; left:7px; } .ds-plate__rivet--tr { top:7px; right:7px; }

components.name: Panel Section
components.description: The generic enamel wrapper used for every content section (services, steps, about, reviews, contact).

narrative.overview:
Every generated site is one business's own truck door, lettered at highway scale and parked on the homepage. The world refuses both the stock-photo local-business template and its gradient-SaaS opposite: no cover photos, no hero illustrations, nothing borrowed from an asset pack. Depth comes from paint and rivets, not glass — enamel panels are built as three-stop radial gradients with a faint diagonal sheen, business names carry a hard signpainter drop-shade instead of a blurred box-shadow, and every plate is bolted down with a symmetric pair (or quad) of rivets at its corners.

The page is built once as a reusable grammar and re-skinned per business: the enamel hue, the gold accent, and the business's own name/trade/city facts change from site to site; the shade-offset lettering, the rivet-and-chip hardware, the reserved-for-calling orange, the type pairing, and the panel/reveal motion do not. That split is the product — fifty generated sites should read as fifty trucks from the same fleet, never as one template with find-replace.

On a phone, the page has one job: get a call placed. A sticky call bar is always visible, the hero panel breaks its own frame to bleed a full-width orange call panel right under the lettering, and a final call panel closes the page. Safety orange is a verb here, not a color — the instant something isn't a phone call, it isn't orange.
keyCharacteristics: Enamel-and-rivet materiality: every panel is a lit/base/deep radial gradient plus rivet hardware, never a flat fill
Hard, offset signpainter drop-shadow on display type — depth from paint, not blur
Orange reserved exclusively for tel: actions; everywhere else the palette stays navy/cream/gold
Alfa Slab One for identity and headline moments, Barlow Semi Condensed for everything else
One-shot, prefers-reduced-motion-gated motion: a single specular glint on load, a staggered panel reveal, a scroll-linked shade deepening — nothing loops

rules.name: The Orange-Is-a-Verb Rule
rules.body: Safety orange (--call / --call-deep) appears only on elements that place a phone call. It never decorates, highlights, or accents.

rules.name: The Per-Business Triplet Rule
rules.body: Every enamel ground is a three-stop radial gradient (lit → base → deep) built from one business hue, never a flat single fill. Re-theming a new business means swapping the three hex values that feed the gradient, not the gradient geometry.

rules.name: The Slab-for-Identity Rule
rules.body: Alfa Slab One is reserved for identity and headline moments — the business name, section headings, and the big painted numerals (ratings, stats, step numbers). Barlow Semi Condensed carries every other word on the page.

rules.name: The Typed-Caps Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the page uses text-transform. Every all-caps moment (the tagline, the since badge, the arc text, the call lead-in) is typed in caps in the source content itself. A generator populating business facts into these slots must supply pre-cased strings, not rely on CSS.

rules.name: The Paint-Not-Glass Rule
rules.body: Depth reads through hard, offset text-shadow and layered radial-gradient enamel. Soft blurred box-shadows are reserved for small, literal physical objects (a rivet's bolt-head, a button's raised edge) — never used as ambient page depth.

rules.name: The Rivet-Pair Rule
rules.body: Any bordered plate (doorframe, trust plate, since-badge) gets rivets in a symmetric pair or quad at its corners — 2 or 4, never 1 or an odd count.

rules.name: The Once-and-Settle Rule
rules.body: The hero's specular glint sweeps exactly once on load; each panel reveals exactly once, then unobserves itself. Nothing on the page loops.

dos: Do reserve safety orange strictly for tel: call actions (The Orange-Is-a-Verb Rule).
Do build every enamel surface as a three-stop lit/base/deep radial gradient plus the faint diagonal sheen overlay — enamel is never a flat fill.
Do type labels and taglines in caps directly in the content, with letter-spacing between .14em and .34em; never reach for text-transform: uppercase.
Do pair rivets at symmetric corners on any bordered plate (doorframe: 4, trust plate: 2, since-badge: 2).
Do stagger panels that enter the viewport together (up to 3 steps, 110ms apart, capped at 330ms) and drop straight to instant-visible under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do keep the phone number legible at every breakpoint — the callbar hides the trade word before it ever truncates the number.
donts: Don't use orange anywhere except a call action — no orange badges, borders, icons, or link states.
Don't blur the signpainter drop-shadow into a soft glow; it must stay a hard offset (paint, not glass).
Don't introduce photography. The world is built from paint, inline-SVG line icons (26px, 2px stroke, gold), and type — no raster imagery anywhere in the shipped page.
Don't loop or repeat the glint sweep or panel reveal; both are one-shot, prefers-reduced-motion-gated animations.
Don't widen the content column past 1060px; every band (door, plates, sections, split) shares that single max-width.
